messages.author: 4dee24c578d7691c
messages.subject: #Cross validation for spatial model question
parts:
Sunday morning thin-plate splining!! What a life.

Feel free to tune out at this point if spatial stuff in R is NOT your cup of tea.

Anyway, I'm working on creating a spatial model for microclimate based on fine-resolution topography data - so far using the Tps() - fields package - and interpolate() - raster package - functions. I'm interested in trying to examine error in my model in as many ways as possible at this point - cross-validation and data partitioning are some ways to do this. I'm curious if the spatial folks might have "favorite" packages / functions out there for this sort of thing.

Any feedback much appreciated! :)

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: #Cross validation for spatial model question
parts:
Hi Stella, 

Can you be more specific?  Are you looking for alternatives to Tps() to relax/evaluate its modeling assumptions (additive errors, degree, etc) or examine errors under these assumptions?  

It looks like Tps does cross-validation to choose its smoothing parameter already, but it looks like one could create a quick cross-validation routine by subsetting your input data, passing to Tps, and comparing the outputs of `predict`.  

I've never used the fields package before, but I think it's difficult to say anything useful without knowing more about the model and research objectives?  (Folks with more expertise in this stuff could no doubt say something more precise)  

- Carl
